public_rationale: Census data from December 14, 2025 to May 3, 2026 show U.S. business AI use between 17% and 20%, with differing trends by firm size; they do not establish a broad demand shortfall ([e2](https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html)). In its July 29, 2026 report for the quarter ended June 30, Microsoft said Azure and other cloud-services demand exceeded capacity ([e1](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2026/earnings-fy-2026-q4)). Reuters reported spending-related investor pushback against Amazon and Microsoft on February 5, 2026, while describing strong Amazon enterprise demand and investor acceptance of Google's spending plans ([e3](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amazon-shares-tumble-200b-ai-004315025.html)). That report does not establish backlash caused by a broad demand shortfall across all three firms ([e3](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/amazon-shares-tumble-200b-ai-004315025.html)).
limitations: Cloud-services demand is broader than AI demand.
The Census survey measures U.S. use in any business function, not global demand or the depth of adoption.
The evidence does not establish the required demand shortfall followed by revenue-driven backlash across all three companies.
No deadline was specified; temporary market resilience cannot settle the forecast.

conditions: if AI adoption slows or demand never arrives

statement.excerpt: In the event that adoption slows — or, more accurately, demand never arrives — Microsoft, Amazon and Google only have so long before the markets sour on their "it's the future, we swear!" messaging, demanding real revenue to match their multi-billion dollar infrastructural bets.

our_interpretation: The antecedent concerns a broad AI-demand shortfall, not merely one product or one disappointing quarterly estimate.
I preserve both formulations: a sustained adoption slowdown could qualify without demand literally disappearing.
The predicted consequence is investor backlash against the three named companies because AI demand and resulting revenue fail to justify their infrastructure commitments.
This assesses conditional investor behavior, not a specified company revenue amount or accounting measure.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented broad AI-demand slowdown or failure to materialize, investors materially mark down all three named firms or press them to retrench, explicitly because revenue does not justify AI infrastructure spending.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After that antecedent is established, a completed, clearly attributable market adjustment shows the opposite response across the named firms. Temporary resilience alone cannot falsify an unlimited 'eventually' prediction.

evidence.explanation: Microsoft's report weighs against demand having failed to arrive. It covers Azure broadly and cannot establish the AI-adoption trend across all three companies.

Some sectors showed little adoption growth, while the same report describes overall growth and differences by firm size. The U.S. survey measures any business-function use, so it does not establish the broad demand shortfall required here.

The report documents investor resistance to spending and adverse reactions involving Amazon and Microsoft. It also describes strong enterprise demand and differing reactions to Google, so it does not establish the claimed conditional chain across all three firms.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable demand or adoption data establishing a broad, sustained slowdown or failure of demand, followed by revenue-driven investor backlash against Microsoft, Amazon and Google, would support the forecast.
